title: In 1964 two Bell Labs engineers could not get rid of a hiss.
description:
In 1964 two Bell Labs engineers could not get rid of a hiss. Arno Penzias and Robert Wilson were using a 20 foot horn antenna at Holmdel. After allowing for the sky and their equipment, 3.5 K of noise was left.

They checked everything, including the pigeons. They removed pigeons nesting in the antenna and cleaned out the droppings. The noise remained.

How much more intense the signal was than they had expected, according to the National Historic Landmark nomination.

Princeton physicists were about to go looking for it. Robert Dicke's group, about 60 km away, was preparing to search for this radiation. Penzias heard of a related preprint from his friend Bernard Burke, then called Dicke.

Both teams published together in July 1965. Penzias and Wilson's short paper ran in Astrophysical Journal Letters straight after the Princeton paper.

They won the 1978 Nobel Prize in Physics. Half went to Penzias and Wilson jointly for the discovery. The other half went to Pyotr Kapitsa.

A noise they could not remove turned out to be the discovery.

Sources:
- https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Discovery_of_cosmic_microwave_background_radiation: read. Established that in 1964 Penzias and Wilson were experimenting with a supersensitive 6 metre (20 ft) horn antenna; a 3.5 K residual background noise after accounting for a 2.3 K sky component and a 0.9 K instrumental component; that they removed pigeons nesting in the antenna and cleaned out the droppings and the noise remained; that Dicke, Peebles and Wilkinson at Princeton, 60 km away, were preparing to search for it; that Bernard Burke told Penzias of a Peebles preprint and Penzias then called Dicke; and that Penzias and Wilson's paper ran at pages 419 to 421 of Astrophysical Journal Letters 142 in July 1965, straight after the Princeton paper.
- https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Holmdel_Horn_Antenna: read. Established the site at Holmdel, that it was built in 1959 for Project Echo, and that it was designated a National Historic Landmark in 1989.
- https://www.nobelprize.org/prizes/physics/1978/summary/: read. Established the 1978 Nobel Prize in Physics: one half to Pyotr Kapitsa and the other half jointly to Arno Penzias and Robert Wilson for their discovery of cosmic microwave background radiation.
- https://npgallery.nps.gov/NRHP/GetAsset/NHLS/89002457_text: read. Established the 1964 to 1965 period of significance, that the noise remained after thorough checking, that the Princeton group was about 40 miles away, and that the signal was 100 times more intense than they had expected.
